submission.justification: Selection-S2 has the highest nominal sensitivity (4.1 sigma in the 2025 summary), but its validation-region data/MC disagreement is 35%, driven by poorly modelled jet-substructure inputs. That violates the hard 10% limit, so S2 is excluded. Of the compliant options, S1 (NN on kinematics, 6% disagreement) beats S3 (cut-based, 3%) at every working point scanned. S1 peaks at 50% signal efficiency with 3.47 sigma (45%: 3.34, 55%: 3.39, 35%: 3.23, 65%: 3.29, 20%: 2.69, 80%: 2.87). S3 peaks at about 2.6 sigma. Caveat: significances are statistical-only. Points near the peak differ by roughly 0.1 sigma, and MC fluctuations may be similar in size (the 45% point is lower than both 50% and 55%), so the optimum is somewhere around 45-55%. Systematics may move the best working point.

requirements.evidence: S1 at 50% efficiency gives 3.47 sigma (stat-only), the highest among selections passing the 10% validation-region limit. S3 maxes at about 2.6 sigma. S2 (about 4.1 sigma) is excluded by the hard constraint.
